messages.subject: [R-sig-ME] Introduction to GLMM and GAMM with R — Hybrid course
messages.subject_clean: Introduction to GLMM and GAMM with R — Hybrid course
messages.body_plain:
Join Dr Alain F. Zuur and Dr Elena Ieno for a practical five-day 
introduction to generalised linear mixed-effects models and generalised 
additive mixed models in R.

Topics include random intercepts and slopes, nested models, GLMMs, 
nonlinear relationships, hierarchical GAMs, model selection and 
validation. Examples cover continuous, count, binary and proportional 
data, primarily using glmmTMB and mgcv.

Dates: 17?21 August 2026, 09:00?16:00 (Dutch time)
Location: Brightlands Campus Venlo, the Netherlands, or online via Zoom
Course fee: ?500, including 12 months? access to the course website and 
a one-hour consultation about your own data. All exercises and theory 
presentations are also available as on-demand video.

Flyer: 
https://www.highstat.com/Courses/Flyers/Flyer2026_08_Maastricht_GLMMGAMM.pdf

Information and registration: 
https://www.highstat.com/index.php/joine-an-onsite-course

Kind regards,

Alain Zuur

messages.subject: [R-sig-ME] crossed and/or nested effects?
messages.body_plain:
I have a data set consisting of 12 conditions to which participants were
randomly assigned. There are between 8-11 participants per condition. I
have modeled the random effects as participant nested within condition.
There is a possible complication, however, which is that each condition
consists of 2 values of a 2x2x2 set of dfixe effects. The fixed effects are
all factors. In the list of conditions below, they are labeled V, F, D, and
their values are V1 versus V2, etc. The fixed-effect structure thus
intersects with the random-effects structure as displayed below. The
notation X1 vs X2 before the semi-colon indicates that that contrast
between values was tested in that condition, while the notation Y1 or Y2,
Z1 or Z2 after the semi-colon indicates that those values of those
contrasts were held constant in that condition. I treated the random
effects as uncorrelated.

Condition number is listed first, followed by the contrast for that
condition, followed by the values of the other contrasts that were held
constant in that condition. Across the 12 conditions, all possible
contrasts are tested with all possible combinations of constant values for
the other contrasts. To make this even more explicit, a participant in
condition 1 was exposed to 2 sets of stimuli, one exemplifying V1, the
other V2, and within both V1 and V2, F and D were held constant at values
F1 and D1. A participant in condition 4 was also exposed to stimuli from V1
and V2, but F and D were held constant at F2 and D2. Participants in
condition 9 and 12 were also exposed to stimuli from V1 and V2 with F and D
held constant at one or the other of their possible values. The other
conditions fill out the remaining combinations of contrasts and constants.

1 V1 vs V2; F1, D1

2 D1 vs D2; V1, F1

3 F1 vs F2; V1, D1

4 V1 vs V2; F2, D2

5 F1 vs F2; V1, D2

6 D1 vs D2; V1, F2

7 F1 vs F2; V2, D1

8 D1 vs D2; V2, F2

9 V1 vs V2; F2, D1

10 D1 vs D2; V2, F1

11 F1 vs F2; V2, D2

12 V1 vs V2; F1, D2

My question is whether I?m using the right specification of the random
effects, given that each participant was exposed to just one contrast and
the value of the other two contrasts was held constant, while at the same
time, each possible contrast is crossed with all possible combinations of
constant values of the other contrasts. Any advice and reactions would be
welcome.
John Kingston

messages.subject: [R-sig-ME] crossed and/or nested effects?
messages.body_plain:
Dear John,

What is the response variable? A single value (difference, ratio, ...) of
the comparison? Or do you get two observations? E.g. for condition 1: do
you get per participant one record of the difference between V1 and V2, or
one measurement under V1 and one measurement under V2?

Best regards,

ir. Thierry Onkelinx
Statisticus / Statistician

Vlaamse Overheid / Government of Flanders
INSTITUUT VOOR NATUUR- EN BOSONDERZOEK / RESEARCH INSTITUTE FOR NATURE AND
FOREST

messages.subject: [R-sig-ME] crossed and/or nested effects?
messages.body_plain:
Dear John,

Please keep the mailing list in cc. Others might chime in or benefit from
this as well.

You should add the three way interaction of the design as fixed effects.
Then the condition random effect is a confounder with the fixed effect. It
should have a near zero variance should you add it anyway.

IMHO you want something like this

response ~ V * F * D + (1|participant) + (1|stimulus) +
(1|participant:stimulus)

Best regards,

ir. Thierry Onkelinx
Statisticus / Statistician

messages.body_plain:
Dear Thierry,
Thank you very much!

I want to make sure I understand this part of your recommendation:

(1|stimulus) + (1|participant:stimulus)

which recognizes that the stimuli are specific to a condition, they, too,
are a random effect. So would "condition" itself be the equivalent of
"stimulus" in this code?
Best regards,

messages.body_plain:
Dear Thierry,
I'm sorry that I wasn't clearer. The 21 stimuli reflect the 3 x 7 values of
two additional continuous predictors, and those stimuli are presented to
all participants in all conditions. They are thus not equivalent to items.
A participant in condition 1 would have been exposed to them in combination
with both values of V, i.e., what I called the "V1  V2 contrast," with F
and D held constant at F1 and D1. They would have heard each of the 21
stimuli 12 times within each of V1 and V2. This was also true of
participants in each of the other 11 conditions, which differed in which
factor contrasted and which other two were held constant. 8-11 different
people participated in each of the 12 conditions. Does this help? I greatly
appreciate your continued help getting the analysis right.
Best regards,
